messages.subject: gl2geno vs gl2structure + struct2geno
parts:
Hi, 
I have a problem regarding my loci count when it comes to execute some function in the LEA package (snmf and lfmm).

I have been using two different strategies to export my genlight data to the geno format in order to get the right number of loci when using those two functions: 
  1. Using the dartR function gl2geno()
  2. Using the dartR function gl2structure() followed by the LEA function struct2geno()  which is kind of a detour, I agree.
Both strategies lead to the same outcome : R console states that I have 27 234 loci when running the snmf function and lfmm also gives me a vector of the same length. However, the true number of loci in my genlight is 15 308 (after several filtering functions) : 
 > s5
 /// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////

 // 270 genotypes,  15,308 binary SNPs, size: 47.6 Mb
 78252 (1.89 %) missing data

 // Basic content
   @gen: list of 270 SNPbin
   @ploidy: ploidy of each individual  (range: 2-2)

 // Optional content
   @ind.names:  270 individual labels
   @loc.names:  15308 locus labels
   @loc.all:  15308 alleles
   @position: integer storing positions of the SNPs
   @pop: population of each individual (group size range: 6-78)
   @other: a list containing: loc.metrics  ind.metrics  loc.metrics.flags  verbose  history 

Is there a possibility that something is not exported properly ?
I'm trying to explain the reason for this random number of loci I get every time.
I also wrote to the creator of the LEA package and he suggests it might be related to the converting step.

I'm using the 2.0.4 version of the dartR package. 
Many thanks,

Alice

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: gl2geno vs gl2structure + struct2geno
parts:
Hi Alice,

There was a bug in the function, which I fixed. To use this updated version of the function you should install the developing version of dartR by typing in the R console:
> library(dartR)
> gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour = "dev")

Cheers,
Luis
